title: Model architecture-specific performance notes (Llama/Mistral/Qwen, long-context, MoE routing)
content:
Summary:

Notes from early-stage investigations into architecture-specific performance characteristics across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen family models, plus observations for long-context execution and MoE routing overhead. This doc is a living working note (mostly raw profiler output + interpretation). Objective is to identify reproducible bottlenecks and short actionable optimizations for the serving runtime.

Goals:
- Surface model-architecture-specific hotspots (memory, kernel time, CPU-side preprocessing, kernel launch overhead).
- Compare latency/throughput behavior across Llama/Mistral/Qwen on common hardware profiles.
- Document long-context scaling behavior and KV cache pressure points.
- Measure MoE routing cost and variance under different expert counts and batch shapes.

Testbed (baseline):
- HW: 8x A100 80GB (single-GPU runs use 1xA100), PCIe config, 2x Xeon Platinum control plane.
- SW: serving-runtime v1.18.1 (local build), CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN versions pinned.
- Models: Llama-2-13B (fp16), Mistral-7B (fp16), Qwen-14B (fp16), MoE prototype based on Mistral-7B with 16 experts.
- Inputs: short prompt (~32 tokens), medium (~256 tokens), long (~4096 tokens).
- Batch shapes: single-request (batch=1), batch=8, batch=32 for throughput.
- Metrics collected: p95 latency, median latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, DRAM usage, GPU memory breakdown, kernel-level timeline (ns).

Tools & methodology:
- nvprof / Nsight Systems for kernel timelines and host/GPU overlap.
- CUPTI traces aggregated into timeline UI.
- Custom sampling of runtime event spans (kernel launch, attention, ffn).
- Prefix KV cache profiling: measure memory growth and memcpy times for cache warm-up and reuse scenarios.
- MoE routing trace: per-token routing decisions logged (sparse index compute + scatter/gather time).

High-level findings (short):
- Llama-2-13B: predictable kernel pattern; attention + ffn dominate. Good kernel fusion; prefix cache works well for long-context but KV memcpy can spike on first warm-ups.
- Mistral-7B: denser FFN (wider inner dim) => higher per-layer GEMM cost relative to attention, but fewer layers can yield slightly lower latency for short sequences. Kernel launches more numerous (smaller GEMMs) leading to CPU launch overhead at very low batch sizes.
- Qwen-14B: larger rotary/position encoding paths + larger head counts cause attention kernels to be heavier; GPU memory footprint higher. For long-context, Qwen shows more memory bandwidth pressure.
- Long-context (>= 2048): KV cache management and KV concat/memcpy dominate host time when sequence lengths are long and batch>1. Observed ~15-30% of end-to-end latency attributable to device<->host copies for cold prefixes.
- MoE routing (16 experts): routing overhead is non-trivial (~10-40% extra latency depending on sparsity and batch shape). Scatter/gather and dynamic dispatch kernels are the main cost; load imbalance across experts leads to tail latency variance.

Detailed observations by architecture:

1) Llama-2-13B:
- Dominant time spent in attention softmax+bmm and FFN GEMMs. Typical kernel breakdown (batch=1, 256 tokens): attention 46%, ffn 42%, tokenization + pos encoding 4%, other overhead 8%.
- Good amortization when batch>1; continuous batching strategy yields ~1.7x tokens/sec moving from batch=1 to batch=8 on our runtime.
- Long-context behavior: p95 increases superlinearly after 2048 due to KV concat memcpys and larger attention matmul shapes. Observed host-to-device memcpy spikes during first long-prefix request: 200–400ms depending on prefix size.
- Actionables: pre-allocate KV buffers for max expected context length in dedicated pools; improve async memcpy pipelining to better overlap KV transfers with compute.

2) Mistral-7B:
- FFN-heavy layout: inner dim ratio larger (wider MLPs), leads to heavy GEMM kernels (two large GEMMs per layer). On A100 these run efficiently but suffer from kernel-launch overhead when GEMM sizes fall below optimal shapes.
- Observed many small kernels for attention & FFN when using sequence lengths < 128; CPU-side launch overhead measured ~20–50us per kernel which adds up. For batch=1, 32 tokens, p50 latency worse than Llama for same model-size.
- Scaling: For medium sequences (256–1024), Mistral benefits from fusing small linear ops; we measured ~10–15% latency reduction after enabling fused MLP kernel in experimental build.
- Actionables: implement a fused MLP kernel path (reduce kernel count), tune kernel-size thresholds for cuBLAS Lt or CUTLASS paths.

3) Qwen-14B:
- Attention head count & rotary embedding implementation increases memory traffic and kernel complexity. Attention kernels dominate at long sequence lengths.
- Memory footprint: Qwen uses ~8–12% more GPU memory than Llama-13B for same sequence due to extra buffers for position/rotary and per-head intermediate buffers.
- Observed bandwidth saturation for long-context 4096 tokens, tokens/sec drops ~25% vs 2048 due to memory-bound attention matmuls.
- Actionables: evaluate compressed rotary representations or streamable rotary computation to reduce intermediate buffer allocations; check opportunity for attention tiling to reduce peak memory footprint.

4) Long-context (general):
- KV cache strategy: two major cost centers: host side concatenation/metadata management and device-side larger GEMMs. For multi-request batching with long prefixes, prefix dedup + shallow cache sharing reduces redundant memcopies by up to 40%.
- Observed that continuous batching with prefix-sharing successfully amortizes prefix cost when there is request overlap.
- Actionables: add a prefix-deduping cache at routing layer that coalesces identical prefix keys before scheduling; ensure KV memcpy paths use cudaMemcpyAsync and pinned host buffers.

5) MoE routing (experimental):
- Routing cost split: dispatch index compute (small GEMMs / FC to compute gating logits), top-k selection & softmax, scatter/gather for expert inputs, per-expert compute, then gather.
- Measured overhead (single-GPU, batch=8, seq=256): routing overhead 18% of total time with 16 experts, per-expert compute 65% (rest baseline). With higher expert counts and lower per-expert load, overhead increases due to many small expert kernels and scatter/gather inefficiency.
- Load imbalance: non-uniform routing causes some experts to be hot; observed tail latency spikes when single expert receives disproportionate load.
- Memory/fragmentation: per-expert activation buffers cause memory fragmentation and allocation overhead when experts are dynamically sized per-batch.
- Actionables: implement static per-expert workspace pooling, asynchronous per-expert execution queues to hide scatter/gather, and a simple load-aware routing fallback to limit max tokens per expert per batch.

Micro-bottlenecks and misc notes:
- CPU-side scheduling: for small batch sizes, host scheduling overhead (enqueuing kernels, handling small memcpy ops) is a consistent ~5–12% of latency across models. Investigate batching of dispatcher operations in the runtime.
- Kernel fusion: where possible, fusing (attention projection + qkv reorder) reduces launches and memory traffic. We have an experimental fused QKV path showing ~8–12% end-to-end improvement on Llama and Mistral in short-sequence runs.
- Mixed precision and quantization: int8 kernels help throughput but can increase per-token latency due to dequantize/quantize conversions; best suited for high throughput, not low-latency single-shot.
- CUDA graph warm-up: using CUDA graphs reduced overhead for repeated identical shapes (batch+seq) by ~15% p50, but is brittle across dynamic shapes. Good candidate for dedicated reserved capacity where request shapes are stable.

Recommendations (prioritized):
1) Short-term (1–2 sprints):
  - Pre-allocate KV buffers and pinned-host buffers to eliminate cold-copy spikes.
  - Land fused MLP kernel for Mistral paths (experimental patch exists in GH-PR-4123).
  - Add prefix-deduping coalescer in routing layer for long-context workloads.
2) Mid-term (1–2 months):
  - Implement static per-expert workspaces + async per-expert queues for MoE.
  - Add attention tiling & streamed rotary computation for Qwen long-context.
  - Expose continuous-batching knobs to customer config for Dedicated (tradeoffs: latency vs throughput).
3) Long-term (quarter+):
  - Investigate tighter CUDA-graph integration across commonly used shapes and provide a cheap fallback when shapes vary.
  - Explore quantization-aware fused kernels for both Mistral and Qwen to balance throughput/latency tradeoffs.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How often do customer workloads require unpredictable long prefixes (>=4096) vs stable shapes? Need telemetry from Console.
- For MoE, is 16 experts the right sweet spot for our typical request mix? Run synthetic sweeps across sparsity and expert counts (4,8,16,32) and measure tail latency.
- Evaluate end-to-end user impact: measure quality delta when applying fused/quantized kernels (QA required).

Action items:
- Asha: instrument prefix-deduping prototype into routing layer (JIRA-ENG-998) and run A/B on synthetic long-context traces.
- Liam: continue fused MLP performance patch and add CITs for small-sequence shapes (GH-PR-4123).
- María: run MoE expert-count sweep and gather per-expert load histograms; produce a short memo with recommended expert counts.
- Ethan: collect Console telemetry for distribution of sequence lengths in Hosted API in last 90 days.

Appendix (sample profiler snippets):
- Example kernel timeline (Llama, batch=1, seq=256):
  - cudaMemcpyAsync (host->device) 18ms (initial prefix)
  - attention_bmm_nt 42ms
  - ffn_gemm_1 34ms
  - ffn_gemm_2 26ms
  - final_layernorm 6ms
- MoE per-stage times (single run): routing_logits 6ms, topk_select 4ms, scatter 10ms, expert_compute (aggregate) 120ms, gather 9ms.

This doc will be iterated; save follow-ups and attach raw traces in GH-PR-4123 where possible.

Notes to self: keep working-run traces with pinned host buffers enabled and without to show delta; test with both CUDA-12.1 and 12.2 where customers will upgrade.
summary: Working notes capturing architecture-specific profiling and recommendations across Llama/Mistral/Qwen, long-context KV behavior, and MoE routing overhead. Contains actionables and owners.
